title: A finite surjective morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme gives a coherent sheaf whose pushforward is supported on a given integral closed subscheme
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], with $X$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z$ an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $\xi\in X$ be the point whose closure $\overline{\{\xi\}}$ is $i(Z)$ (the generic point of $Z$). Then there is a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] such that the direct image $f_*\mathcal F$, $(f_*\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}U)$ [def-pc-module-pullback], satisfies $\operatorname{Supp}(f_*\mathcal F)=\{x\in X:(f_*\mathcal F)_x\neq0\}=i(Z)$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](2), with stalks as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and $\mathfrak m_\xi\,(f_*\mathcal F)_\xi=0$, where $\mathfrak m_\xi$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YO (label lemma-finite-morphism-Noetherian, coherent.tex line 3479)

proof.text: (The point and its reduced closure.) A finite morphism is locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-finite-iff-integral-lft], so $Y$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. Surjectivity gives a point $\xi'\in Y$ with $f(\xi')=\xi$. Put $T=\overline{\{\xi'\}}\subseteq Y$ and give it the reduced induced closed subscheme structure $i':Z'\to Y$ of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The space $T$ is nonempty and irreducible, with generic point $\xi'$, and $Z'$ is reduced; hence $Z'$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YO (lemma-finite-morphism-Noetherian), proof, lines 3490-3496; Schemes, Lemma 01J3 for the reduced induced structure

proof.text: (The image and the map to $Z$.) The continuous map underlying $f$ sends $T=\overline{\{\xi'\}}$ into $\overline{\{f(\xi')\}}=\overline{\{\xi\}}=i(Z)$. On the other hand $f(T)$ is closed because $f$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], and it contains $\xi$; hence it contains $\overline{\{\xi\}}=i(Z)$ and therefore $f(T)=i(Z)$. Since $Z'$ is reduced and the image of $f\circ i'$ lies in the closed subscheme $i:Z\to X$, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] gives a unique morphism $f':Z'\to Z$ with $i\circ f'=f\circ i'$; it is surjective on points because its image maps homeomorphically onto $f(T)=i(Z)$ under $i$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YO, proof and displayed square, lines 3495-3508; the image equality and factorization are implicit in the displayed square

proof.text: (The coherent sheaf.) The closed immersion $i':Z'\to Y$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], hence locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-finite-iff-integral-lft]. Since $Y$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $Z'$ locally Noetherian, and its structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{Z'}$ is coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Thus $\mathcal F=i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'}$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent]. Functoriality of sectionwise pushforward and $i\circ f'=f\circ i'$ give $f_*\mathcal F=f_*i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'}=i_*f'_*\mathcal O_{Z'}$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YO, proof, lines 3495-3510; Lemma 01Y6 supplies coherence

proof.text: (The generic stalk.) Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ containing $\xi$, write $f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be the primes of $\xi$ and $\xi'$. Finiteness says that $B$ is a finite $A$-module, hence integral over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. The reduced closure of $\mathfrak q$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak q)$, so the affine description of pushforward and stalks gives $(f_*\mathcal F)_\xi\cong(B/\mathfrak q)_\mathfrak p$. A prime of $B/\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak r\supseteq\mathfrak q$ of $B$ with $\mathfrak r\cap A=\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$; incomparability for the integral extension [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability] forces $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak q$. Thus the domain $(B/\mathfrak q)_\mathfrak p$ has only the zero prime, so it is a field, necessarily the fraction field $\kappa(\xi')$ of $B/\mathfrak q$. In particular $(f_*\mathcal F)_\xi\cong\kappa(\xi')\neq0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YO, proof, lines 3510-3518; Algebra, Lemmas 00GK and 00GT

proof.text: (Annihilation at $\xi$.) Under the isomorphism of step 4, the $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$-module structure on $(f_*\mathcal F)_\xi$ is induced by the local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}\to\mathcal O_{Z',\xi'}=\kappa(\xi')$. Its kernel contains the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_\xi$, because the induced map on residue fields is $\kappa(\xi)\to\kappa(\xi')$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Therefore $\mathfrak m_\xi(f_*\mathcal F)_\xi=0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YO, proof, lines 3516-3520 ('In particular')

proof.text: (Support.) The sheaf $f_*\mathcal F$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent], hence quasi-coherent of finite type and has closed support [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. From $f_*\mathcal F=i_*f'_*\mathcal O_{Z'}$ and the closed-pushforward stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks], its support is contained in $i(Z)$. It contains $\xi$ by step 4. Since $i(Z)=\overline{\{\xi\}}$, every closed subset of $X$ contained in $i(Z)$ and containing $\xi$ contains all of $i(Z)$. Consequently $\operatorname{Supp}(f_*\mathcal F)=i(Z)$, completing the construction.

split_report.summary: Split Stacks 01YO into six steps: choose a lift of the generic point and its reduced integral closure; identify its closed image with Z and factor through Z; construct the coherent closed pushforward; compute the generic stalk affinely using finiteness, integrality and incomparability; prove maximal-ideal annihilation; and obtain exact support from closedness and the generic point. All non-elementary inputs already have current DAG nodes, so no new node was created. The existing LeanSearch, LeanFinder and Mathlib-source grep all give no match.
